searchText: Can I get some editor feedback on https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2494 ? <@!425279588009246720> it sounds like you are able to confirm that `xlab` is one of the authors for https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2765 so I'll leave it to you to merge that (and I recommend helping the user update the email address to GH username as well). We *really* need to get the EIP bot to not listen in on forks. Does anyone have any idea how to fix that? The bot just recently pinged like 30 people: <https://github.com/vorot93/EIPs/pull/104> because someone merged master into their fork (essentially). <@!301186049323958275> Left a comment on 2494. I'm re-opening basically all of the auto-close-warning issues <@!425279588009246720>. I realize now that this bot's job was to trick me into addressing all of these Draft EIPs by putting them in my inbox. 😢 So much for getting real work done today... Why are you reopening them? My takeaway is that we should have enable the bot once eipv has stronger checks in place, like checking for missing sections 🙂 Because that is one the notorious issues with all the pending drafts. <@!301186049323958275> I do not think you should review all the stale marked ones before the author pings that they are still interested. Otherwise this defeats the purpose. > Why are you reopening them? <@!425279588009246720> I'm "touching" them because no editor actually asked for any changes originally, and so the bot's suggestion to close them or "fix the suggested edits" isn't reasonable. The majority of them fail on CI, so they were not even valid before editor comments. > I do not think you should review all the stale marked ones before the author pings that they are still interested. Otherwise this defeats the purpose. <@!425279588009246720> Hmm, you think we should just leave them with no editor feedback and just the bot telling them to respond to the editor feedback? I feel like there should be a bot complaining that "hey look, this fails ci, no editor will respond until that is fixed" Ah, true. I guess I could limit my commentary to EIPs that at least pass CI. I think you get an email from Travis if you fail CI? Oh, probably only if you have a Travis account... Though one peculiar problem is that CI fails in every case because of the filename and missing number field, but I usually ignore that CI error and still comment, unless there are other major CI errors. So there's no good solution apart from making eipv check for sections, etc. and making a bot which displays the findings of eipv as comments on the PR. Should we disable the bot for the time being? Also I think using the github suggestions is a two edged sword: it makes it easy for submitters to click merge and hence making merging easy. In many cases they would not go to actually do the change themselves if they were only comments, which begs the question whether they will follow up after it is merged as a draft 🤔 > Should we disable the bot for the time being? <@!425279588009246720> No, I don't think so. > Also I think using the github suggestions is a two edged sword: it makes it easy for submitters to click merge and hence making merging easy. In many cases they would not go to actually do the change themselves if they were only comments, which begs the question whether they will follow up after it is merged as a draft 🤔 <@!425279588009246720> If the user has been ignoring feedback I probably won't merge. My suggestions and intention to merge after suggestions applied are for the ones where the user did everything right and the only reason their EIP isn't Draft is because *we* (editors) didn't do the right thing and give them prompt feedback. As someone who has had an EIP sit waiting on editors for over a year, I can appreciate their frustration at following all of the rules and still getting no progress. It is frustrating from all parties. People seriously struggle with git, and in many cases it takes them weeks to follow up (even when responding promptly at the time of submission, in my experience), and a handful of back and forth comments to get the validation to pass. My frustration is that almost nobody looks at the red CI mark, likely because they are unfamiliar with git -- hence we should have a bot post the issues from eipv. And because of this delay of them responding, it is often forgotten when they respond given the hundreds of other notifications. It is just really hard to manage this at 200 open PRs. Well, I definitely struggle 🙂 I've looked at "botifying" eipv, but it is painful because it is in Rust (<@543900561460822016> 👀). Could not find a working github actions / API crate for rust, while all of them exists for python / js / ts / ruby. > <@!425279588009246720> it sounds like you are able to confirm that `xlab` is one of the authors for https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2765 so I'll leave it to you to merge that (and I recommend helping the user update the email address to GH username as well). <@!301186049323958275> I asked him to include the username or mark it abandoned, but he was reluctant to add the username and asked not to abandon it 😕 Is @xlab in GitHub the same as one of the authors? (I don't know them, so I cannot confirm personally) The way I look up the username is the following (and I **should not** be doing this): - `git blame` the file to check its commit hash - `get show <hash>` and see what was the PR number - check the PR on github and see what was the username originally submitting the EIP - and usually ping that username Ah, and that process revealed this user is in fact one of the authors? If so I'll propose a suggestion to update the appropriate author to GitHub username. Well that user submitted the EIP in the first place 🙂 So I assume must be the author? Do we know which author is them? Oh, GitHub tells me their name. The first one, if you click on the username you get the name Got it, thanks. Since we rely on github, the automerger, etc. I think we should just require github username (at least one per EIP) and discourage emails as this is getting rather tiresome in many cases. I support that. Even if someone responds to an email request, how is the editor supposed to prove that? Copy paste the email verbatim into the PR? Yeah, I agree with the "one GitHub author per EIP minimum". And no way I have the time to reach out on email pinging people. > We *really* need to get the EIP bot to not listen in on forks. Does anyone have any idea how to fix that? The bot just recently pinged like 30 people: <https://github.com/vorot93/EIPs/pull/104> because someone merged master into their fork (essentially). <@!301186049323958275> I have no idea how the automerger was triggered there I don't have any idea where the automerger lives or runs, but I'm almost positive the issue is that it is watching all EIP repository forks. My *guess* is that it is run by CI in a file in the EIPs repository (e.g., Travis) and then when a fork is created Travis sees that fork and starts running CI against it. It is pinged by travis and apparently there's no check for repo in the automerger: https://github.com/eip-automerger/automerger/issues Btw it is linked in the EIPs repository README 🙂 I can't be bothered to read fluff material like the README! 😛 Anyway good job on the reviews! Hopefully it is sustainable haha I think once we get the PR count down it will become more sustainable. Especially with the auto-close thing you setup. Actually on the autoclose, I think we may want to tune it: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2949#issuecomment-689032064 Now we need a full time person implementing the fixes for eipv/automerger 🙂 We do need someone on-"staff" who *can* fix the automerge bot. <@!425279588009246720> Am I incorrect that the whole process starts over from 0 days as soon as anyone comments on the EIP? I did an automerger fix myself last year (to include the PR number in the commit log), but that was enough python for me. > <@!425279588009246720> Am I incorrect that the whole process starts over from 0 days as soon as anyone comments on the EIP? I think that's how it works, that's why I suggested different time limits. Although it ignores comments from bots apparently. I support your suggested limit changes. Looks like lightclient as well, I say YOLO it. 😉 If you scroll up to yesterday, I posted some logs from the stale bot. And it seems to think I'm a bot too, so perhaps ignores my comments 🤷‍♂️ Beware you may be considered a bot soon too, and be ignored by the stale bot haha After reviewing a bunch of ERCs what I miss in many drafts is a description of a flow how the interface is supposed to be used. It seems to be a recurring issue. I mean those which practically define state machines. Most ERCs are terrible IMO. I *really* want to get them out of the EIPs repository. 😖 Like 90% of them IMO are just someone defining their app's API or just describing their app. They have no need to be standardized. It is a good way to shill 🙂 Yeah. 😕 So I'm starting to get into the EIPs that are pretty old (from last year)... I'm really hesitant to touch them and reset the bot timer, but at the same time I really hate that the bot's message says "please respond to the editor feedback" when there was no editor feedback... In hindsight, I wish I would have thought about that before suggesting the bot message wording I did. 😢 Should have just kept the vague one I had 🙂 Like this one, EIP has no feedback on it, and then a year later it is marked as stale: <https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2368> Also, this one had discussion and comments and is green in GitHub and ready for merge, but for some reason it just never was merged: <https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2348> https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2444 and https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2467 are good examples are ERCs lacking clarity on the specification front Re: <https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/2467#issuecomment-689505234> I dislike that style, but understand why it is used. I really wish Solidity would have put visibility and modifiers before the parameter list. 😢 I dislike using solidity in ERCs but there's no better alternative (I proposed one, but it is not as "expressive" and "accessible"). Meh, Solidity doesn't bother me. People use C++, or Python, or even JavaScript in specifications all the time and I think it makes it appeal to a *much* wider audience that way than some esoteric language that no one knows. I am truly torn on whether to just archive all of these email notifications, or try to work my way through them. I was planning on rewriting 2718 plus a few other EIPs today and ended up spending all my free time today just doing EIP reviews from the bot's mass closure list. After realizing I was only on page one of two... I'm starting to think I should just archive all and wait for people to comment. Also, there are a bunch that I *hope* the author doesn't pursue... I share the sentiment, I would rather not spend time on reviving dead endeavours, unless someone is persistent. btw, that was ruthless on #2467, but needed 🙂 I'm surprised you kicked 2430 down the road. > btw, that was ruthless on #2467, but needed 🙂 😬 I did feel bad writing it, the person has put some effort into writing the spec and trying to follow all of the rules. <@!425279588009246720>, what sort of things were you wanting to "botify"? I was thinking that the existing bot could read the result of `eipv` and just post the errors to the PR?

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content: I was thinking about making use of github actions as it seems to be working well and there are frameworks to write them -- except for rust. Then I'd run the validator and create individual comments for those using github actions.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yes the automerger

excerpts.author: axic3354
excerpts.content:
The problem with the automerger is that both the repository and the deployment (on google appengine) is controlled by Nick and he's just busy with other things.

Actually thought about rewriting the automerger as a github action too, as then it would be completely controlled via the repository and removing the need for this external trigger.

excerpts.author: lightclient
excerpts.content: yep, makes sense

excerpts.author: axic3354
